ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, O is the center, and there are points E, F, H, P, Q, G, etc. on the circumference; O is the South Pole in the question. In the figure there is one vertical radius in the up-down direction and one horizontal diameter E—O—F. H and P are located in the upper part of the circle, respectively on the two sides of the upper vertical radius, and the angles with the upper vertical radius are both marked as 20°, so H and P are symmetrical about the upper vertical radius, and the central angle corresponding to the upper short arc between H and P is 20°+20°=40°. Reasoning: According to the question, H and P are two intersections of the terminator line and a certain latitude, so the upper short arc between H and P can be judged as the short night arc on that latitude. A short night and long day indicate that the Southern Hemisphere has longer days than nights; and since O is the South Pole, it indicates that the Southern Hemisphere is facing the sun, and the date should be around December 22. The midline of the night arc corresponds to local time 0:00, that is, the upper vertical radius in the figure is the 0:00 meridian. Point F is located at a position 90° clockwise from this 0:00 meridian. For every 15° difference in longitude, local time differs by 1 hour, 90°÷15°/hour=6 hours, so the time at point F is 6:00. Combining the date, the time at point F may be 6:00 on December 22.

raw_record.question_text:
Read the figure and complete the following questions.

<image1>

If O is the South Pole, and H and P are two intersections of the terminator line and a certain latitude, then what time may it be at point F?

method.method_draft: 先从图中确定 H、P 关于上方竖直半径对称，夹角为 20°+20°，所以 H、P 之间的上方短弧是晨昏线在该纬线截出的短夜弧。结合题干 O 为南极点，短夜长昼说明南半球向阳，应取 12月22日前后。短夜弧的中线，即上方竖直半径，是地方时 0 时。F 位于从该 0 时经线顺时针相差 90°的位置，90°÷15°/h=6h，因此 F 点时间为 12月22日6时。

In the figure there is one vertical radius in the up-down direction and one horizontal diameter E—O—F. H and P are located in the upper part of the circle, respectively on the two sides of the upper vertical radius, and the angles with the upper vertical radius are both marked as 20°, so H and P are symmetrical about the upper vertical radius, and the central angle corresponding to the upper short arc between H and P is 20°+20°=40°. Reasoning: According to the question, H and P are two intersections of the terminator line and a certain latitude, so the upper short arc between H and P can be judged as the short night arc on that latitude. A short night and long day indicate that the Southern Hemisphere has longer days than nights; and since O is the South Pole, it indicates that the Southern Hemisphere is facing the sun, and the date should be around December 22. The midline of the night arc corresponds to local time 0:00, that is, the upper vertical radius in the figure is the 0:00 meridian. Point F is located at a position 90° clockwise from this 0:00 meridian. For every 15° difference in longitude, local time differs by 1 hour, 90°÷15°/hour=6 hours, so the time at point F is 6:00. Combining the date, the time at point F may be 6:00 on December 22.
